mainTopic: The law of a מתעסק on שבת and in other איסורים, רבי יוסי on work done at בין השמשות, and when an אשם תלוי is brought.
overview: The גמרא first asks which case the rule 'a מתעסק is exempt' is about. It answers that the rule teaches a specific שבת case, which differs for אביי and רבא depending on how much intent to cut is needed. Next it explains רבי יוסי's claim that work done at בין השמשות is פטור because it is split across two days. He holds to this even for a quick lifting. רב יוסף then answers a question from רבי אליעזר's weaving rule. The גמרא then turns to the אשם תלוי. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the same פסוק differently, and a ברייתא proves that רבי שמעון requires an אשם תלוי even when it is unclear whether one sinned at all. Finally, שמואל rules that a מתעסק is liable for חלבים and עריות because he had pleasure, but exempt on שבת because only מלאכת מחשבת is forbidden. He defends this rule against two challenges: the case of the two babies, which is about wounding, and the case of picking the wrong fruit.

steps.title: Which case is the exemption talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which area of law the ruling 'a מתעסק is exempt' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ruling that one who acts unawares is exempt: what case is it about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a question about the earlier ruling that a מתעסק is exempt. This sets up the next two steps, which test the possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק is someone who does an act without meaning to do the forbidden thing at all. The גמרא wants to know which איסור such a person is exempt for, because each option it tries will run into a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: One who acts unawares, doing a forbidden act without meaning to do it

phrases.english: One who acts unawares — regarding what?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which איסור the exemption of a מתעסק applies to.

steps.title: It cannot mean forbidden fats or forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling is about חלבים or עריות, that is wrong, because שמואל rules that a מתעסק there is liable since he enjoyed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about forbidden fats and forbidden relations, he is liable! As רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: one who acts unawares with forbidden fats or forbidden relations is liable, because he got pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, חלבים and עריות, and rejects it using a ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With eating and relations, the body gets pleasure even if the person did not mean to sin. Because of that pleasure, שמואל holds that even a מתעסק must bring a קרבן. So the exemption cannot be talking about these איסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (here, to bring a קרבן חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a מתעסק is always exempt. For חלבים and עריות, שמואל holds he is liable because of the pleasure.

phrases.english: If it is about forbidden fats and forbidden relations — he is liable,
as Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
One who acts unawares with forbidden fats and forbidden relations is liable,
since he got pleasure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the exemption refers to חלבים and עריות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that a מתעסק with חלבים and עריות is liable because he got pleasure, so an exemption cannot be talking about them.

steps.title: For שבת the exemption is already obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling is about שבת, it is not needed, because we already know the תורה only forbids מלאכת מחשבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is about one who acts unawares on שבת, he is exempt anyway. Why? The תורה forbade only planned work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second possible answer, שבת, and argues that the exemption there is already known, so there is no reason to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת the תורה only forbids מלאכת מחשבת, work done with intent. A מתעסק has no such intent, so of course he is exempt. If so, the ruling would be teaching us nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Planned, intended work, the only kind of work the תורה forbids on שבת

phrases.english: And if it is one who acts unawares on Shabbat — he is exempt anyway,
What is the reason?
The Torah forbade only planned work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first option failed, this tests the second option and finds it unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the exemption refers to שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The principle of מלאכת מחשבת already exempts a מתעסק on שבת, so teaching it again would add nothing.

steps.title: It refers to a specific שבת case, different for רבא and אביי
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is about שבת, but it teaches a less obvious case. For רבא, he meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one. For אביי, he meant to lift a detached plant and cut an attached one.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא, you find it where he meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one. According to אביי, you find it where he meant to lift a detached plant and cut an attached one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling is about שבת after all. It teaches a specific case that is not obvious, and that case depends on whether you follow רבא or אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא places the exemption in the case where he himself holds the person is exempt. רבא exempts even someone who meant to cut, as long as he did not mean to do a forbidden cutting. אביי holds that person is liable, so for him the exemption must be about someone who only meant to lift the plant.

keyTerms.meaning: You find it, meaning the case where this ruling applies
Detached, a plant already picked from the ground
Attached, a plant still growing in the ground

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'מתעסק on שבת' is not one simple case. How much intent a person had changes whether he is exempt.

phrases.english: According to Rava, you find it
phrases.notes: 'It' means the case where the exemption for a מתעסק is actually needed.

phrases.english: for example, where he intended to cut the detached plant
and he cut the attached one.
According to Abaye, you find it
for example, where he intended to lift the detached plant
and he cut the attached one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 3 by naming a שבת case where the exemption teaches something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the ruling to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מתעסק on שבת is obviously exempt, so the ruling teaches nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling teaches a borderline שבת case: for רבא, intending to cut a detached plant; for אביי, intending to lift one.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: meant to lift, but cut, is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the source behind the answer. Someone who meant only to lift a detached plant and accidentally cut an attached one is exempt, because he had no intent to cut at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: if he meant to lift a detached plant and cut an attached one, he is exempt. Why? Because he did not intend any cutting at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the cases it just mentioned, starting with the case that everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting a detached plant is not a מלאכה at all. Since this person had no thought of cutting, the cutting that happened is purely accidental, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of any cutting at all

phrases.english: As it was stated: if he intended to lift the detached plant
and he cut the attached one, he is exempt,
What is the reason?
Because he did not intend any cutting at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for אביי's case in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's case of a מתעסק: meant to lift, cut instead
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement quoted with דאיתמר, where everyone agrees this person is exempt

steps.title: The dispute: meant to cut a detached plant, but cut an attached one
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he is liable because he meant to cut. רבא says he is exempt because he did not mean to do a forbidden cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one: אביי says he is liable, because he meant to cut. רבא says he is exempt, because he did not mean a forbidden cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the quoted source with the case that אביי and רבא argue about. This explains why each of them placed the exemption in a different case in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the person meant to cut something. אביי says intent to do the act of cutting is enough to make him liable. רבא says he must have intended a forbidden cutting, and cutting a detached plant is permitted, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden cutting, cutting that the תורה actually forbids

steps.whatToRemember: Meant to lift and cut instead: everyone says exempt. Meant to cut a detached plant and cut an attached one: אביי says liable (he meant to cut), רבא says exempt (he did not mean a forbidden cut). That is why each places 'מתעסק is exempt' in a different case.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא do not argue about the lifting case. They only argue when the person actually meant to cut.

phrases.aramaic: לַחְתּוֹךְ אֶת הַתָּלוּשׁ וְחָתַךְ אֶת הַמְחוּבָּר –
phrases.english: If he intended to cut the detached plant and he cut the attached one:
Abaye said: he is liable,
because he did intend to cut.
Rava said: he is exempt,
because he did not intend a forbidden cutting.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַחְתּוֹךְ אֶת הַתָּלוּשׁ וְחָתַךְ אֶת הַמְחוּבָּר – אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted source with the case that אביי and רבא dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intending to cut a detached plant but cutting an attached one: אביי says liable because he meant to cut; רבא says exempt because he did not mean a forbidden cutting.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view and his reply to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's line from the משנה. Then it brings a ברייתא where he tells the חכמים, 'You examined me closely.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: They did not disagree, etc. It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said to them: You examined me closely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting רבי יוסי's opinion in the משנה. It adds a ברייתא with a short, puzzling remark he made to the חכמים, and the next step will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי says both sides agree that work done at בין השמשות is פטור, because part of it was 'today' and part was 'tomorrow.' The ברייתא shows the חכמים pushed back on this. The words 'you examined me closely' tell us they found something to challenge, and steps 8-9 explain what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for 'and so on.' The rest of the quoted line is not written out
You examined me closely, meaning you looked hard for a weak spot in my words

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
They did not disagree, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה line: work done at twilight is exempt, since part was done today and part tomorrow.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei said to them:
You examined me closely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, everyone agrees that a מלאכה done at בין השמשות is פטור, because it is split across two days.

steps.title: What did the חכמים say to him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what challenge the חכמים raised that made רבי יוסי say, 'You examined me closely.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they say to him, that he said to them: You examined me closely?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the חכמים said to רבי יוסי. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only רבי יוסי's reply and leaves out the question that came before it. The גמרא wants to rebuild that missing question.

phrases.english: What did they say to him
that he said to them: You examined me closely?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background of the ברייתא quoted in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What question from the חכמים led to רבי יוסי's reply?

steps.title: They asked about lifting at בין השמשות
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים asked about someone who lifted an object at בין השמשות. רבי יוסי answered, 'You examined me closely.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they said to him: If he lifted at בין השמשות, what is the law? He said to them: You examined me closely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The חכמים asked about lifting an object at בין השמשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason was that a מלאכה at בין השמשות is split across two days. Lifting an object happens almost instantly, so it seems to happen in one moment and not across two days. That is why the question was a sharp one.

keyTerms.meaning: He lifted, picking up an object as part of carrying it
Twilight, the in-between time when it is unclear which day it is

phrases.english: This is what they said to him:
If he lifted at twilight, what is the law?
He said to them: You examined me closely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים asked about lifting at בין השמשות, a quick act that seems not to stretch over two days.

steps.title: Why didn't he say lifting is also split?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי didn't simply answer that part of the lifting was today and part tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say to them: Part of the lifting was today and part of it was tomorrow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's reply. It asks why he didn't use his usual reason for lifting too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי holds that בין השמשות is split between two days, even a quick lifting could fall partly on each day. So it seems he had an easy answer, and his remark sounds like he was giving in.

keyTerms.meaning: Tomorrow, here meaning the next day

phrases.english: But let him say to them:
part of the lifting was today
and part of it tomorrow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's reply 'You examined me closely'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own reason, that the work is split across two days, should apply to lifting too, so why did he seem to give in?

steps.title: He meant: your question gained nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי's full reply was: 'You examined me closely, and you gained nothing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what he is saying to them: You examined me closely, and you have not brought up anything in your hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי did not give in. His full words were, 'You examined me closely, but you came up with nothing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the answer the קשיא suggested. Even lifting is split between the two days, so the חכמים' question does not break his rule. He praised their effort but kept his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, that is indeed the case
You did not bring up anything in your hands, meaning you gained nothing

phrases.english: That is indeed what he is saying to them:
You examined me closely,
and you have not brought up anything in your hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completes the quote: his reply had a second half that rejected the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי admitted the lifting case was a problem for him
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי held that even lifting is split across two days, so the challenge failed
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי stands by his rule. Any מלאכה at בין השמשות, even a quick lifting, is split across two days, so the person is פטור.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר really exempt finishing a מלאכה?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוסי, רבי אליעזר exempts someone who finished a מלאכה on one day. But we know רבי אליעזר holds a person liable for finishing a מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי, for completing a מלאכה, רבי אליעזר holds he is פטור? But we have heard that he holds him liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on רבי יוסי. He claims that even רבי אליעזר agrees the person is פטור, and the גמרא doubts this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's picture, only part of the work, at most the finishing part, happens on any one day. Yet elsewhere רבי אליעזר holds a person liable even when he only finished a מלאכה. So how could רבי יוסי say that רבי אליעזר agrees he is פטור?

keyTerms.meaning: The finishing of a forbidden labor
But we have heard him say

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei, for completing a labor,
according to Rabbi Eliezer he is exempt?
But we have heard that he holds him liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי גְּמַר מְלָאכָה, לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge to רבי יוסי's claim that רבי אליעזר agrees
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that רבי אליעזר also exempts work done at בין השמשות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר holds a person liable for just finishing a מלאכה, so splitting the work across days should not make him פטור

steps.title: Proof from weaving one thread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי אליעזר holds a person liable for weaving one thread onto existing cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי אליעזר says: One who weaves three threads at the start, or one thread onto a woven fabric, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim in step 12. It is a משנה about weaving on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally weaving needs three threads to make a person liable. But רבי אליעזר holds him liable even for one thread added to existing cloth, because that thread finishes the work. This shows he treats finishing a מלאכה as enough to make someone liable.

keyTerms.meaning: At the beginning, starting a new piece
A fabric that is already woven

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who weaves three threads at the beginning,
or one onto a woven fabric, is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 12
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר holds a person liable for just finishing a מלאכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת שבת about weaving one thread onto existing cloth

steps.title: רבי יוסי had a different version of the weaving teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that according to רבי יוסי, רבי אליעזר requires two threads on existing cloth, not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי יוסי, following רבי אליעזר, taught it this way: רבי אליעזר says one who weaves three threads at the start, or two threads onto existing cloth, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question from Steps 12-13. He says רבי יוסי had a different version of the weaving משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that רבי אליעזר seems to make a person liable for adding just one thread to finish a cloth. רב יוסף says that in רבי יוסי's version, רבי אליעזר requires two threads on existing cloth. So the משנה from Step 13 is no longer a contradiction to רבי יוסי's report of רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches, meaning he has the text in this version
One who weaves (a מלאכה on שבת)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָכִי מַתְנֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, according to Rabbi Eliezer, teaches it this way:
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי had his own wording of the weaving משנה quoted in Step 13.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who weaves three threads at the beginning,
or two onto already-woven cloth, is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָכִי מַתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised from the weaving משנה in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the source text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר makes a person liable for one thread added to cloth, so he holds a person liable for finishing a מלאכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבי יוסי's version, רבי אליעזר requires two threads on existing cloth, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: רבי יהושע exempts even from an אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי יהודה says רבי יהושע exempts even from an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: רבי יהושע would exempt him even from an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes the next line of the משנה. It is setting up the ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, the person knows he sinned but does not know what he sinned with. רבי יהושע already exempts him from a חטאת. רבי יהודה adds that רבי יהושע exempts him even from the lighter אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'hanging' or provisional guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Rabbi Yehoshua would exempt him
even from a provisional guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the רבי אליעזר discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, רבי יהושע exempts this person from an אשם תלוי too.

steps.title: The verse source for רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the פסוק behind רבי יהודה: an אשם תלוי is only for someone who does not know whether he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said that רבי יהושע exempts him even from an אשם תלוי, because the פסוק says 'if he sins and does not know.' That leaves out this person, who knew that he sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק behind רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads 'ולא ידע', 'and does not know', as 'he does not know whether he sinned at all.' Our person does know he sinned. He only does not know with what, so the אשם תלוי does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹטְרוֹ הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אַף מֵאָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua would exempt him even from a provisional guilt offering,
as it is said: "If he sins and does not know"
This leaves out this person, who knew that he sinned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse source for the משנה line quoted in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי is only for someone who does not know whether he sinned. Not for someone who knows he sinned.

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads the same verse the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that this person does bring an אשם תלוי, because the פסוק speaks of one who does not know what he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: This is exactly the one who brings an אשם תלוי. The פסוק says 'he did and does not know,' and this person does not know with what he sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה and uses a phrase from the same פסוק to prove the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads 'ועשה ולא ידע' as 'he did something and does not know what it was.' That describes our person exactly: he sinned but does not know with which item. So he brings an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: And he did and did not know (words of the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sages quote the same פסוק. רבי יהודה stresses 'did not know' as not knowing whether he sinned. רבי שמעון stresses 'did and did not know' as not knowing what he did.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
This is the one who brings a provisional guilt offering,
as it is said: "And he did and did not know,"
and this one did not know with what he did it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: זֶהוּ שֶׁמֵּבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהודה's conclusion that someone who knows he sinned is exempt from an אשם תלוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק says 'he did and did not know,' which fits someone who does not know what he sinned with.

steps.title: רבי שמעון leaves the pure doubt case open
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that when it is unclear whether one ate forbidden fat at all, the law must still be asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is unclear whether he ate forbidden fat or did not eat it, go and ask whether he brings an אשם תלוי or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. Here רבי שמעון does not decide a different case, where it is not even clear that the person sinned. Steps 19-21 settle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's proof covered someone who surely sinned but does not know with what. Here there is a complete doubt whether any sin happened. His reading of the פסוק does not clearly settle this case, so he leaves it open.

keyTerms.meaning: Go and ask, meaning this question is left open

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל סָפֵק אָכַל חֵלֶב סָפֵק לֹא אָכַל –
phrases.english: But if it is unclear whether he ate forbidden fat or did not eat it,
go out and ask about it

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אִם לָאו.
phrases.english: whether he brings a provisional guilt offering or not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל סָפֵק אָכַל חֵלֶב סָפֵק לֹא אָכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי שמעון's words in the ברייתא and raises an open case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this ברייתא, רבי שמעון does not decide the case of a pure doubt whether one sinned. Step 21 settles it.

steps.title: What was decided about the open question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final answer is for רבי שמעון in the case of a pure doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the open question from the ברייתא was settled. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'go and ask.' Now the גמרא wants to know what רבי שמעון actually holds about someone who may not have sinned at all.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the answer to the question left open in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון require an אשם תלוי when it is unclear whether one sinned at all?

steps.title: A ברייתא that puts both cases together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that both someone who does not know with what he sinned and someone who may not have sinned bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he sinned and does not know with what he sinned, or if it is unclear whether he sinned at all, he brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. It is setting up a proof about רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא puts the two cases side by side and gives both the same ruling. The next step will show whose opinion this ברייתא follows.

keyTerms.meaning: He sinned and does not know with what he sinned
It is unclear whether he sinned or did not sin

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he sinned and does not know with what he sinned,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ סָפֵק חָטָא סָפֵק לֹא חָטָא –
phrases.english: or if it is unclear whether he sinned or did not sin,
he brings a provisional guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's view on a pure doubt whether one sinned
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that requires an אשם תלוי in both cases

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, so he requires an אשם תלוי even in a pure doubt
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי שמעון requires an אשם תלוי for one who does not know with what he sinned. So the ברייתא is his, and he also requires it for a pure doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who do we know says that one who sinned and does not know with what brings an אשם תלוי? רבי שמעון. And this ברייתא teaches that one with a doubt whether he sinned brings an אשם תלוי. Learn from this that רבי שמעון holds that one with a doubt whether he sinned brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון, and so it settles the open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling in the ברייתא is רבי שמעון's well-known view against רבי יהודה. So the whole ברייתא is his, including the second ruling. That means רבי שמעון also requires an אשם תלוי when it is unclear whether one sinned at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have we heard say this? (a way to identify whose opinion a source follows)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון requires an אשם תלוי both for one who sinned without knowing with what, and for one who is unsure whether he sinned at all. רבי יהודה exempts the first case.

phrases.english: Whom have we heard who says:
one who sinned and it is not known with what he sinned
brings a provisional guilt offering?
Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: From Step 17, where he argued with רבי יהודה over exactly this case.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא תָנֵי: סָפֵק חָטָא סָפֵק לֹא חָטָא –
phrases.english: And it teaches: if it is unclear whether he sinned or did not sin,
he brings a provisional guilt offering.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: סְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Learn from this: Rabbi Shimon holds:
if it is unclear whether he sinned or did not sin,
he brings a provisional guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in Step 20 by identifying its author.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון holds that one who is unsure whether he sinned brings an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: The משנה's final clause: the פסוק excludes a מתעסק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's statement that רבי שמעון and רבי שמעון שזורי say there was no argument in a certain case. It also quotes the משנה's conclusion that the פסוק 'אשר חטא בה' comes to exclude a מתעסק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי and רבי שמעון say: they did not argue, etc. If so, what does the פסוק 'wherein he has sinned' come to teach? It comes to leave out someone who acts unawares.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the last part of the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the next step, which explains the law of a מתעסק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה holds that when both items are the same kind (for example, both are fats), the person is liable even if he mixed them up. That leaves the question of what the words 'אשר חטא בה' are for. The answer is that they exempt a מתעסק, someone who never meant to do a forbidden act at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who does a forbidden act without meaning to do that act at all

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri and Rabbi Shimon say
They did not disagree, etc.
If so, what does the verse come to teach
'wherein he has sinned'?
To exclude one who acts unawares.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of רבי שמעון's view on a pure doubt to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'אשר חטא בה' exempts a מתעסק from a חטאת.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: a מתעסק is liable for fats and forbidden relations but exempt on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל rules that a מתעסק is liable for forbidden fats and forbidden relations because he had pleasure. On שבת he is exempt, because the תורה forbids only planned work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: someone who acts unawares with forbidden fats or forbidden relations is liable, since he had pleasure. Someone who acts unawares on שבת is exempt, because the תורה forbade only thought-out work.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains where the exemption for a מתעסק applies and where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With eating and relations, the body still enjoys the sin even if the person did not mean to do it, so he is liable. On שבת the rule is different: what is forbidden is מלאכת מחשבת, planned work. A מתעסק did not plan anything, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Planned, intended work, which is the only kind the תורה forbids on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key split between kinds of sins. Where pleasure is involved, intention matters less. On שבת, intention is part of what makes it a sin.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
One who acts unawares with forbidden fats or forbidden relations is liable,
since he had pleasure.
One who acts unawares on Shabbat is exempt,
for the Torah forbade planned work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the exemption for a מתעסק from the previous step reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מתעסק is liable for forbidden fats and forbidden relations because he had pleasure. He is exempt on שבת because only מלאכת מחשבת is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא brings the case of the two babies
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן with a משנה. A man had two babies, one due for מילה on שבת and one after שבת, and by mistake he circumcised the second one on שבת. רבי אליעזר says he owes a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: what about the case of the babies, which is like a case of acting unawares? We learned: someone had two babies, one to be circumcised on שבת and one after שבת. He forgot and circumcised the after-שבת baby on שבת. רבי אליעזר says he must bring a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a challenge against שמואל's rule by quoting a משנה. The full point of the attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man meant to do a permitted מילה, so his forbidden act was not what he intended. That makes him similar to a מתעסק on שבת. Yet רבי אליעזר holds him liable, and רבי יהושע's exemption still needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: It is similar to, it is like

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
But what about the case of the babies,
which is like one who acts unawares,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי תִּינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: and we learned: one who had two babies,
one to circumcise on Shabbat
and one to circumcise after Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת בַּשַּׁבָּת –
phrases.english: and he forgot and circumcised the after-Shabbat one on Shabbat –
Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable to a sin offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן וְהָא תִּינוֹקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's rule that a מתעסק on שבת is exempt.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a מתעסק on שבת is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man who circumcised the wrong baby on שבת is like a מתעסק, yet רבי אליעזר holds him liable to a חטאת.

steps.title: Even רבי יהושע would hold a regular מתעסק liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא sharpens the challenge. רבי יהושע exempts only because the man made a mistake while doing a מצוה. In a case with no מצוה, even רבי יהושע would hold a מתעסק liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע exempts here only because he holds that someone who made a mistake about a מצוה, and did not end up doing a מצוה, is exempt. But someone who acts unawares in a matter that is not a מצוה, even רבי יהושע holds liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his challenge. Both opinions in the משנה seem to hold that a regular מתעסק on שבת is liable, which goes against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא blocks the answer that שמואל could simply follow רבי יהושע. רבי יהושע's exemption comes from a special reason, a mistake made while busy with a מצוה, and not from a general exemption for a מתעסק. So no one in the משנה supports שמואל's exemption on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He only says this here, in this specific case
He made a mistake while doing a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יהושע as agreeing with שמואל. רבא's whole point is that רבי יהושע's exemption comes only from the מצוה factor and not from being a מתעסק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge puts שמואל's rule for שבת in danger, and רב נחמן defends it in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פָּטַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua exempts only here
because he holds:
one who erred in a matter of a מצוה
and did not end up doing a מצוה is exempt,
but one who acts unawares in a matter that is not a מצוה –
even Rabbi Yehoshua holds him liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פָּטַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's challenge by showing that רבי יהושע's exemption cannot support שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a מתעסק on שבת is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע exempts only because a מצוה was involved. That implies a regular מתעסק on שבת is liable according to both opinions, which goes against שמואל.

steps.title: Wounding is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא: the babies' case proves nothing. With wounding, even a destructive act is liable, so even a מתעסק who wounds is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave the babies aside. Since one who wounds destructively is liable, one who wounds without meaning to is also liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge from the case of the two babies (step 24-25). He says that case is about wounding, and wounding follows its own rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally on שבת a destructive act (מקלקל) is exempt. Wounding (חבורה) is an exception: even a destructive wound makes one liable. Since wounding already breaks the usual rules, it is also no surprise that a מתעסק who wounds is liable. That says nothing about other forbidden work on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who damages or destroys; normally exempt on שבת
Wounding, making a wound that draws blood
One who does an act without meaning to do the forbidden thing
Leave aside; the case is not a proof

phrases.english: He said to him: Leave the babies aside,
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering רבא's challenge from the two babies' מילה.

phrases.english: since one who damages by wounding is liable,
one who acts unawares in wounding is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by limiting the babies' case to wounding.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof to an exceptional category (wounding)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא thought the babies' case shows that any מתעסק on שבת is liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only in wounding is a מתעסק liable, because wounding is liable even when destructive. Other work on שבת still needs a planned act.

steps.title: A new challenge from picking the wrong fruit
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes a משנה against שמואל. Someone meant to pick one fruit and picked another; רבי אליעזר makes him bring a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה challenged שמואל. רבי יהודה says: Even if he meant to pick figs and picked grapes, or grapes and picked figs, or black ones and picked white, or white and picked black, רבי אליעזר makes him bring a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה brings a new source to challenge שמואל's rule that a מתעסק is exempt on שבת. Here he only quotes the source; the actual point of the attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a person who picked a different fruit than the one he planned. That sounds like a מתעסק, since he did not mean to pick what he picked. The list of cases sets up the attack, which depends on what רבי יהושע exempts and what he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: To pick or harvest; a forbidden labor on שבת
Holds him liable to bring a sin-offering

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda raised an objection to Shmuel:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even if he intended to pick figs
and he picked grapes,
or grapes, and he picked figs,
or black ones, and he picked white ones,
or white ones, and he picked black ones –
Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable to a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the babies' challenge is answered, a new challenge to שמואל's rule begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a מתעסק on שבת is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about picking the wrong fruit seems to deal with a מתעסק, and yet רבי אליעזר holds him liable.

steps.title: Even רבי יהושע would hold him liable within one type
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's point: this person is a מתעסק. רבי יהושע exempts only when the fruit switched to a different type, so within one type even רבי יהושע holds him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here he is a מתעסק! And even רבי יהושע exempts only when he switched from one type to another. Within one type, even רבי יהושע holds him liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה now spells out why the משנה is a problem for שמואל. Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע would hold a מתעסק liable in at least some case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only lists switches between types (figs and grapes, black and white). That implies a switch within the same type is liable even according to רבי יהושע. So no one in the משנה holds that a מתעסק on שבת is always exempt, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: From one type to another type
Within one and the same type

phrases.english: But here he is one who acts unawares,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נָמֵי לָא קָא פָטַר
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua too does not exempt him
except from one type to another type,
but within one type –
even Rabbi Yehoshua holds him liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the attack based on the משנה quoted in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a מתעסק on שבת is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the picker is a מתעסק, then רבי אליעזר always holds him liable, and רבי יהושע holds him liable within one type. So both hold a מתעסק liable on שבת in some case.

steps.title: שמואל reads the משנה as a forgetful picker
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה to drop his reading of the משנה. The case is a picker who first wanted grapes, then forgot and thought he wanted figs, and his hand took grapes anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Sharp one, leave the משנה and follow me. What case are we dealing with here? The picker lost track in his mind. He intended to pick grapes, then forgot and thought: I want figs. And his hand went onto the grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by explaining that the משנה is not about a regular מתעסק at all. It is about a special case where the person's thoughts changed in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's case, the grapes he picked are exactly what he first planned to pick. So this is not a simple מתעסק who grabbed something he never wanted. The argument in the משנה is only about this mixed-up case. A regular מתעסק stays exempt according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'big-toothed one'; a nickname for a sharp student
What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrow reading of a source)
Lost track in his mind; forgot what he had planned

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the picker grabbed grapes when he wanted figs all along. He first wanted grapes, then switched in his mind to figs, and his hand took the grapes he had first wanted.

phrases.english: He said to him: Big-toothed one,
phrases.notes: שמואל is answering רב יהודה with a friendly nickname, his way of calling him sharp.

phrases.english: leave the mishna and come follow me,
what are we dealing with here?
for example, where the picker lost track in his mind,
he intended to pick grapes,
and he forgot, and thought: It is figs I want,
and his hand went onto the grapes,

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: שיננא, שבוק מתניתין ותא בתראי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's challenge by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the source as a narrow case (הכא במאי עסקינן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה thought the משנה was about a plain מתעסק who picked the wrong fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a picker whose plan changed from grapes to figs, and who then picked grapes after all.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds him liable because his original intention (grapes) was carried out. רבי יהושע exempts him because his current intention and thought (figs) was not carried out.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אליעזר holds: his intention was carried out. And רבי יהושע holds: his intention and thought were not carried out.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל finishes his answer by explaining the reasoning on each side of the argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר looks at the first plan: he wanted grapes and got grapes, so he is liable. רבי יהושע looks at what he was thinking at the moment of picking: figs, which he did not get, so he is exempt. Neither side is talking about a plain מתעסק, so שמואל's rule that a מתעסק on שבת is exempt still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: His intention, what he meant to do
His thought, his plan at that moment

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule survives. A plain מתעסק on שבת is exempt according to everyone. The fruit-picking argument is only about someone whose plan changed partway through, and wounding is a special exception where even a מתעסק is liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is about which intention counts, the original plan or the current thought. It is not about whether a מתעסק is liable.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Eliezer holds:
his intention was carried out,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
his intention and thought were not carried out.

steps.triggerLanguage: דרבי אליעזר סבר: הרי נעשתה כוונתו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's answer by giving each sage's reasoning in the case he described.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the argument as about which intention counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that a מתעסק on שבת can be liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is only about original plan versus current thought, so a plain מתעסק stays exempt.
